Increase each even digit by 1.
Decrease each odd digit by 1.

Arrange in descending order

9, 8, 7, 6, 5

sum = 9 + 8 + 7 + 6 + 5 = 35

questions.question: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions based on it. There are 2 floors between E and C and 1 floor between E and F. C lives on the first floor. F doesn't live immediately above C. There are 2 people between A and D. D doesn't live on an odd floor. questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions based on it.
There are six people A, B, C, D, E and F who live in a six-storey building, the lowest floor is numbered 1 and the highest is numbered 6. E lives on an even-numbered floor. questions.solution:

2 floors below → 1st floor → C

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: No apple is blue. All oranges are apples. Conclusions: I. No orange is blue. II. Some apples are oranges.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.
Statement:
No apple is blue. All oranges are apples.
Conclusions:
I. No orange is blue.
II. Some apples are oranges.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No orange is blue. → Follow (As no apple is blue and all oranges are apples. So whole oranges comes in apple which cannot be blue, therefore it is true.)

II. Some apples are oranges → Follow (A all oranges are apples. So whole oranges comes in apple, therefore it is true.)

Thus, both I and II follow.

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: All bags are pens. Some pens are not pencils. No pencil is a scale. Conclusions: I. Some bags are not scales. II. All scales are pencils.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.
Statement:
All bags are pens. Some pens are not pencils. No pencil is a scale.
Conclusions:
I. Some bags are not scales.
II. All scales are pencils.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some bags are not scales → Does not follow (As all bags are pens, some pens are not pencils and no pencil is a scale. As no direct relation is given between bags and scale, therefore it is possible but noy definite.)

II. All scales are pencils → Does not follow (As no pencil is a scale. As direct relation is given between pencil and scale, therefore it is false.)

Thus, Neither I nor II follows.

questions.question: A man is 4 times as old as his daughter. In 20 years, he will be twice as old as she will be then. How old is the daughter now?
questions.questionHtml: A man is 4 times as old as his daughter. In 20 years, he will be twice as old as she will be then. How old is the daughter now?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Current ratio (Man:Daughter) = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 units)

Ratio after 20 years = 2 : 1. Make differences equal: multiply by 3 → 6 : 3

Increase in units = 6 − 4 = 2 units. These 2 units = 20 years.

1 unit = 10 years. Daughter's current age (1 unit) = 10 years.

∴ The correct answer is 10 years.

Alternate Method

Given: Present age ratio = 4:1. Ratio after 20 years = 2:1.

Formula Used: Ratio & Proportion linear equations.

⇒ Let Daughter's age = x and Man's age = 4x.

⇒ After 20 years: (4x + 20) = 2 × (x + 20)

⇒ 4x + 20 = 2x + 40

⇒ 4x − 2x = 40 − 20

⇒ 2x = 20

⇒ x = 10

∴ The correct answer is 10 years.

Additional Information

Concept of Age Difference

The age difference between two people always remains constant throughout their lives. This is a key tool in solving ratio-based age problems.

Ratio Balancing

To solve age ratios quickly, multiply the ratios so that the difference between the parts (Man − Daughter) is identical in both current and future ratios.

Linear Equations in Ages

If "n" years ago is mentioned, subtract n from current age; if "n" years hence/later is mentioned, add n to the current age.
